newsitem.title: Philippines: Manila court clears JG Summit petrochem site.
newsitem.headline: Manila court clears JG Summit petrochem site.

text.p: A Philippine Court of Appeals has cleared the way for JG Summit Holdings Inc to build its petrochemical complex in Batangas city, south of Manila, court documents made available on Monday said.

It dismissed for lack of merit the petition filed by Representative Enrique Garcia who had insisted that Bataan province should be the exclusive site of all petrochemical facilities in the country, the documents showed.
The government's Board of Investments (BOI), which grants fiscal incentives to preferred industries, had allowed JG Summit last year to locate its plant in Batangas.
Bataan is about 50 km (31 miles) west of Manila while Batangas is about 100 km (62 miles) south of Manila.
Garcia had claimed the BOI's ruling violated a number of presidential decrees which reserved 576 hectares of land in Limay, Bataan as the country's petrochemical zone.

"While admitting that a petrochemical zone had been established in Limay, Bataan, it does not prevent other petrochemical plants from being established outside Bataan," Associate Justice Romeo Brawner said in a seven-page decision.
"To have an interpretation on Bataan's exclusivity would not only curtail the petrochemical industry's growth but also stunt the industrialisation efforts of the country," Brawner added.

JG Summit had said it would be cheaper for the company to set up its petrochemical plant in Batangas because it owns the land. The Batangas site also offers the advantage of being near the refineries of Caltex (Philippines) Inc and Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp where feedstock for its complex can be sourced.
The petrochemical project is expected to cost 2.346 billion pesos. It will have a naphtha cracker, polyethylene/polypropylene plant, and a polyvinyl chloride plant.
